rules.rule: Treat this as a public compatibility boundary. Check backward compatibility, schema/version evolution, optional-vs-required fields, serialization stability, idempotency fields, UTC timestamp semantics, and accidental leakage of secrets or provider-specific implementation details. Flag breaking changes without an explicit migration/versioning strategy.

Review event contracts as append-only audit/analytics data. Check stable event names and versions, correlation IDs, tenant/workspace scoping, timestamp semantics, PII/secrets leakage, replay safety, duplicate handling, and whether downstream consumers can evolve independently.

Focus on durable workflow correctness: deterministic state transitions, retries/backoff, idempotency, cancellation, concurrency, race conditions, timeouts, partial failure, duplicate delivery, recovery after process crash, and separation between deterministic control logic and non-deterministic AI reasoning.

Focus on external side effects and multi-network publishing: idempotency keys, duplicate publish prevention, rate limits, remote status reconciliation, auth/token handling, scheduling/time zones, retry classification, partial success, platform-specific policy isolation, and canonical-contract-to-adapter translation.

Focus on provider isolation, prompt/tool injection boundaries, model/tool authorization, timeout/retry/circuit-breaker behavior, token/cost controls, redaction, structured output validation, deterministic fallbacks, observability, and prevention of provider-specific types leaking into domain code.

Focus on untrusted media/file handling, command injection, path traversal, temporary-file cleanup, resource limits, cancellation, deterministic outputs, codec/tool failures, GPU/CPU exhaustion, resumability and artifact integrity.

Check that adapters remain replaceable and do not contaminate the core. Verify canonical input/output translation, capability detection, error normalization, retryability classification, version pinning assumptions and contract tests for each external system.

Focus on tenant isolation, authorization, unsafe client trust, XSS/CSRF, upload safety, optimistic update consistency, accessibility, performance regressions and clear handling of long-running asynchronous workflow states.

Treat infrastructure as security-sensitive. Check least privilege, secret exposure, public ingress, network boundaries, persistence/backups, rollout/rollback safety, image/version pinning, resource limits, observability and disaster recovery assumptions.

Review CI/CD for supply-chain security and correctness: pin third-party actions where practical, minimize permissions, protect secrets on forked PRs, avoid executing untrusted PR code with privileged tokens, use concurrency intentionally, cache safely, and keep quality/security gates reproducible.
